decisions.reason: As a close extension of the firm's core cardboard display business, this product is likely to meet internal aspiration levels well enough and a large firm has enough slack to keep such a recent launch on the market.
This is another near-core display variant, so without evidence of clear underperformance management would likely retain it rather than search for alternatives immediately.

A standard quarter-pallet cardboard display fits the firm's established capabilities and customer base very closely, making it unlikely to fall below aspirations strongly enough to be dropped quickly.
The eighth-pallet format broadens the existing display range with little strategic stretch, so a large incumbent would usually keep it while learning about demand.

Because the wooden pallet moves somewhat beyond the firm's paper-based core, it faces higher uncertainty and a greater chance of falling short of aspirations, but the firm's size and service model still make retention more likely than exit.

Although it uses core cardboard-display capabilities, its media-specific focus makes demand more uncertain, so the drop risk is higher than for generic formats but still not high enough to outweigh the firm's slack and recent-launch tolerance.
